domains.name: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System

clusters.name: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers

standards.description: Introduce students to the definition of i and the form a + bi so they can recognize and write any complex number correctly.
standards.ccssText: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = −1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

standards.description: Guide students to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers by applying i² = −1 along with the commutative, associative, and distributive properties.
standards.ccssText: Use the relation i² = −1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

clusters.name: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations

standards.description: Help students solve quadratic equations with real coefficients whose discriminant is negative, expressing solutions as complex conjugate pairs.
standards.ccssText: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

clusters.name: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

standards.description: Lead students through the derivation of the finite geometric series sum formula and apply it to real-world contexts such as financial problems.
standards.ccssText: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate mortgage payments.

domains.name: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

clusters.name: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials

standards.description: Help students apply the Remainder Theorem to evaluate polynomials and determine whether a linear expression is a factor.
standards.ccssText: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

standards.description: Guide students to identify zeros of polynomials from factored form and use them to sketch a rough graph of the function.
standards.ccssText: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

clusters.name: Use polynomial identities to solve problems

standards.description: Support students in proving polynomial identities such as the difference of squares or sum/difference of cubes and using them to describe numerical relationships.
standards.ccssText: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

standards.description: Help students divide polynomials using inspection or long division to rewrite a rational expression in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x).
standards.ccssText: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

clusters.name: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

standards.description: Guide students to write and solve equations and inequalities in one variable arising from linear, quadratic, rational, and exponential contexts.
standards.ccssText: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

domains.name: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities

clusters.name: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning

standards.description: Help students solve simple rational and radical equations and identify extraneous solutions that arise from the solution process.
standards.ccssText: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

standards.description: Guide students to solve systems with one linear and one quadratic equation both algebraically and graphically, interpreting intersection points.
standards.ccssText: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

standards.description: Help students graph square root, cube root, piecewise, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions showing key features such as zeros, asymptotes, and end behavior.
standards.ccssText: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

subStandards.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.
Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.
Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.
Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

clusters.name: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities

standards.description: Help students write functions that model relationships by combining standard function types through arithmetic operations or composition.
standards.ccssText: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

subStandards.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

Compose functions. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

clusters.name: Build new functions from existing functions

standards.description: Guide students to identify how replacing f(x) with f(x) + k, k·f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) shifts, stretches, or reflects the graph for specific values of k.
standards.ccssText: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

standards.description: Help students find inverses of simple functions by solving f(x) = c and writing the inverse expression, understanding when an inverse is also a function.
standards.ccssText: Find inverse functions.

subStandards.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) = 2x³ or f(x) = (x+1)/(x-1) for x ≠ 1.

domains.name: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models

clusters.name: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems

standards.description: Guide students to express the solution to an exponential equation as a logarithm and evaluate it using technology.
standards.ccssText: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab^(ct) = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

clusters.name: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle

standards.description: Help students understand radian measure as arc length on the unit circle so they can interpret and convert angle measures fluently.
standards.ccssText: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

standards.description: Guide students to use the unit circle to define and evaluate trigonometric functions for all real number inputs interpreted as radian measures.
standards.ccssText: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

clusters.name: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions

standards.description: Help students select and fit sine or cosine functions to model real-world periodic phenomena by identifying amplitude, frequency, and midline from context.
standards.ccssText: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

standards.description: Lead students to prove sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find any one of sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given another and the quadrant.
standards.ccssText: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

domains.name: Statistics and Probability — Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data

clusters.name: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

standards.description: Guide students to represent bivariate data on a scatter plot and fit an appropriate function — linear, quadratic, or exponential — to the data.
standards.ccssText: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

subStandards.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

domains.name: Statistics and Probability — Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions

clusters.name: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments

standards.description: Help students understand that statistics is a process of using random samples to make inferences about population parameters.
standards.ccssText: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

standards.description: Guide students to evaluate whether a given model is consistent with observed results by using simulation as a tool.
standards.ccssText: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation. For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

clusters.name: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies

standards.description: Help students distinguish between surveys, experiments, and observational studies, and explain how randomization relates to each method.
standards.ccssText: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

standards.description: Guide students to use sample data to estimate a population mean or proportion and develop a margin of error through simulation.
standards.ccssText: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

standards.description: Help students use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments and use simulations to assess whether observed differences are significant.
standards.ccssText: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

standards.description: Teach students to critically evaluate statistical reports by examining study design, sampling methods, and the appropriateness of conclusions.
standards.ccssText: Evaluate reports based on data.
